solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Upset by locks? You've got them in your sights

definitions.text: You've got them in your sights

parts.note: upset as an adjective means annoyed or cross
locks of hair are hairs

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by their own hair while aiming at a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine lines in a gunsight or telescope that mark the aiming point are seen whenever you look through it.

clue.text: Fake drug regulations

parts.note: cod is British slang for sham or mock, as in a cod accent
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Phoney rules about medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a systematic set of rules or laws, such as a highway code.

clue.text: Opposed settings covering shipping areas when business is slack

indicators.note: the switch positions sit around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the two opposite positions of a switch are off and on
seas are the areas ships travel

explanation.surface: Contrary arrangements about maritime zones at a quiet time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settings' suggests scenery, but the two settings are a switch's positions, placed on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The off season is the quiet period of the year when trade, especially tourism, is low.

clue.text: Instructions for making lamp shades?

definitions.meaning: specifications are detailed instructions for building something
lamps is slang for eyes, so their shades are spectacles

explanation.surface: Directions for building covers for lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lamps' is old slang for eyes, so lamp shades are glasses; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Specs is short both for specifications and for spectacles, the glasses worn over the eyes.

clue.text: Further velocity carried by a ball

indicators.note: the velocity symbol is held inside the next piece

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
V is the symbol for velocity in physics

explanation.surface: Extra speed given by a ball in some sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To further a cause is to advance or promote it; both verbs mean help forward.

clue.text: Composer's baton — kit taken by leader of orchestra

parts.note: a baton is a short rod or stick
kit or equipment is a rig

indicators.note: the first letter of the word orchestra leads it

explanation.surface: A conductor's stick and gear are taken by the orchestra's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer's' is 'Composer is'. Joaquín Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez.
explanation.definitionFit: Joaquín Rodrigo is a famous Spanish composer, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Medium with a lot of animation, on reflection

definitions.text: Medium with a lot of animation, on reflection

indicators.note: a mirror reflection turns the letters back to front

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: most of the word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: animation in the sense of liveliness is life

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, cinema is full of cartoons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns M plus LIF (most of LIFE) backwards. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema is an artistic medium, and much of it is animated, as cartoons are.

clue.text: Former tribesman's preserved?

definitions.meaning: a member of the people who ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest
food sealed in a tin is preserved; split 2,3 the word says in a tin

explanation.surface: Was an old tribal member kept from decay?
explanation.walkthrough: 'tribesman's' is 'tribesman is'. Split as IN CAN the answer means tinned, hence preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan describes a member of the ancient South American empire; read as two words it means tinned.

clue.text: Actor playing Mum or Mam tries it out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or misplaced, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor cast as a mother tries the role of mother or mam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' as a word means silent, so the definition is a silent performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who acts without speaking is literally keeping mum, a silent actor.

clue.text: European politician retains and lives for stress

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
to retain is to have
lives in the sense of exists, is

explanation.surface: A European politician keeps going despite pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress laid on a word or idea is emphasis, a synonym.

clue.text: Brilliant note put out by the same novelist

parts.note: def is slang for excellent or brilliant

indicators.note: the note letter is ejected from the following word

parts.note: one can mean the same, as in one and the same

explanation.surface: A dazzling message delivered by an identical writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the pieces. Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe, author of Robinson Crusoe, is a well-known English novelist.

clue.text: Volume one edited's retracted — keep silent about city guidebook

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: drawn back, so the letters run the other way
the silent word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to keep mum is to keep silent
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A book's edited first volume is withdrawn while the city keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited's' is 'edited is'. EC is the postcode of the City, London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A vade mecum (Latin 'go with me') is a handbook carried for constant reference.

clue.text: City male to fall into line? Not half

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: the falling word is put inside the halved word
only half of the word line is used, its first two letters

parts.note: to sink is to fall

explanation.surface: A man is asked whether to collapse into a queue, and answers 'not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the slang for 'very much' but takes LI, half of 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Male notes a hair colour?

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
NN is the abbreviation for notes, plural of n

explanation.surface: A man remarks on someone's hair shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown plant dye used to colour hair and skin.

clue.text: Refunds brought round for those accused of patronising loose women?

definitions.text: those accused of patronising loose women?

indicators.note: the refunds word is put around the next piece

parts.note: refunds of money are rebates
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Money returned to men charged with using prostitutes.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO also means prostitute, so the definition puns on rebates 'brought round' pros.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprobates are immoral or unprincipled people, the sort one might accuse of keeping low company.

clue.text: Forming unit — redesigned unit, see?

indicators.note: something redesigned is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new combined room: the unit has been redesigned, you see?
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms that are en suite form a single unit, such as a bedroom with its own bathroom.

clue.text: Evil is around in Ohio or somewhere similar

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed round the next two

parts.note: ill means evil or bad, as in ill deeds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wickedness is rife in Ohio or a similar place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ohio' looks part of the definition but only gives its abbreviation; the definition is a US state similar to Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is another Midwestern US state, so it is a place similar to Ohio.

clue.text: Round things rolling around when observed

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape

indicators.note: things rolling about tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Circular objects tumbling about while being watched.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on sight is to act as soon as something is seen.

clue.text: France curtailed its girl's clumsiness

indicators.note: cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Gaul is the old Roman name for the region of France
France's girl, a darling, is a chérie in French

explanation.surface: France, cut short, blames its girl for awkwardness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl's' is 'girl is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaucherie is social awkwardness or tactless behaviour, borrowed from French gauche, left-handed.

clue.text: Footballer runs working business, accommodating 50

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a machine that is working is on

indicators.note: the business word holds the number inside

parts.note: ado means fuss or business
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A footballer runs a working business that houses fifty people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronaldo is a famous footballer, either Brazil's Ronaldo or Portugal's Cristiano.

clue.text: Student fliers, crashing into tree, ultimately take the biscuit?

indicators.note: the fliers go inside the tree, as a plane crashes into it

parts.note: an oak is a tree
the ATC, Air Training Corps, is a British youth organisation for cadet airmen

indicators.note: the final letter of the word take

explanation.surface: Trainee pilots flying into a tree really take the biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the biscuit' is British for being outrageous; the definition is just 'biscuit'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a flat savoury biscuit made of oatmeal, popular in Scotland.

clue.text: Something thrown at second debate

parts.note: a discus is thrown in athletics

explanation.surface: Something hurled at a second argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss a subject is to debate or talk it over.

clue.text: Daughter torn about Independent's description of film

indicators.note: the torn word goes round the next letter

parts.note: riven means torn apart

explanation.surface: A girl ripped up the Independent newspaper's movie review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent's' is 'Independent is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in cinema shows a movie to people seated in their cars, so the term describes how a film is watched.

clue.text: Meat company breaking embargo

indicators.note: the company letters break into the ban, sitting inside it

parts.note: an embargo is a ban

explanation.surface: A meat firm defies a trade ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork meat.

clue.text: Bygone revelry cut short after appearance of copper

indicators.note: the revelry piece comes after the copper piece

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the final letter is removed

parts.note: a riot of fun is wild revelry

explanation.surface: Old-time merrymaking was ended once a policeman arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bygone is an old ornament or antique, as is a curio, a small collectable rarity.

clue.text: Drunk about to leave, finishing early, when the night's still young?

indicators.note: the drunk word goes around the next piece

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: the word ends early, losing its last letter

parts.note: to will is to leave in a will, to bequeath

explanation.surface: A drunk is about to leave early, though the night has barely begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to leave' looks like 'on the point of going' but splits into an indicator and a definition of WILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim period just after sunset, when the night is only beginning.

clue.text: New line supported by a wife chasing one's relative

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the one
in a down entry the supporting pieces sit below

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A new partner backed by a wife pursuing one's relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is 'one is'. In a down answer, 'supported by' puts A and W below N and L.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is a relative by marriage, such as a mother-in-law.

clue.text: Dog heading away from Liverpool suburb

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is dropped

parts.note: Speke is a district of Liverpool, site of its airport

explanation.surface: A dog runs off from a part of Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Speke is a southern suburb of Liverpool, home to John Lennon Airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peke is a Pekingese, a small long-haired breed of dog.

clue.text: Stop boring pest holding one back

indicators.note: the pest contains the next piece

parts.note: a termite bores through wood

indicators.note: the word is turned backwards

parts.note: an means one

explanation.surface: Halt the dull insect holding someone back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' suggests dull but means tunnelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end, to stop it.

clue.text: Former actor swashbuckling colleague brought back?

indicators.note: the name is returned, read backwards

parts.note: Errol Flynn was a swashbuckling Hollywood star and fellow Warner Bros actor

explanation.surface: A retired actor's dashing co-star is recalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Lorre was a Hungarian-born film actor of the 1930s and 1940s, famous in Casablanca.

clue.text: Give away? Not if this business situation is to succeed!

definitions.meaning: to give someone away is to inform on or betray them

explanation.surface: You must not give away the shop if your business is to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to 'giving away the shop', conceding too much in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for betraying them to the police; a shop is also a store.

clue.text: Fail, say, in retracting expression of condolence that's immediately swallowed

indicators.note: drawn back, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: e.g., for example, means say

indicators.note: the comforting word takes the next piece inside

parts.note: 'there, there' is a comforting expression
now means immediately

explanation.surface: Failing, perhaps, while taking back sympathy that is instantly absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To get nowhere is to make no progress, an idiom for failing.
